gap: None of the result pages I could read (Macworld and PCWorld in full, TechRadar and RTINGS only in part) states that a 16-inch 2560x1600 panel works out to 189 ppi, 74% of the 16-inch MacBook Pro's 254 ppi, on a 13.57 x 8.48 in panel that matches the MacBook's 16:10 area (13.61 x 8.50 in) to within 0.04 in, or that a bus-powered 16-inch screen at ASUS's 13 W ceiling takes Apple's 17 wireless-web hours down to about 5.3.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac, which gives 65 W pass-through and 2.9 lb for the Duex Float 2 Pro but no ppi, no monitor wattage, no battery-hours figure, no mention of the 140 W charger and no combined carry weight. PCWorld's roundup says only that a small screen 'increases the display's pixel density' and gives no ppi, wattage or battery hours. TechRadar's roundup loaded only its first pick and RTINGS' loaded no picks, so I could not check those two fully. ChatGPT's own answers warn about battery drain and pass-through with no number. The limit on my finding: the battery arithmetic has a maker's wattage for the ASUS only, and the ppi and size match are identical for every 16-inch 2560x1600 screen, so they justify the line more than they separate the candidates inside it.
decides: It confirms the page's line: a 16-inch 16:10 2560x1600 panel is the same width as the MacBook's screen (13.57 in against 13.61 in), so a screen stacked above it (Duex Float 2 Pro) lines up edge to edge, while a 15.6-inch 16:9 4K panel is denser (282 ppi) but 0.85 in shorter. It also puts numbers on the Duex Float 2 Pro's two costs: 7.6 lb carried with the MacBook, and a 65 W pass-through that is 46% of Apple's 140 W adapter. It does not separate the Duex Float 2 Pro from the UPERFECT GR16DQ or ASUS MB16QHG on sharpness, because all three share the pixel grid; that split falls to brightness, weight and price.

findings.label: MacBook Pro 16 battery hours with the screen bus-powered at the maker's ceiling
findings.value: about 5.3 h of wireless web (from Apple's 17 h, M5 Pro); about 5.8 h of video streaming (from 24 h); about 5.2 h of web on the M5 Max (from 16 h)
findings.note: 100 Wh / 17 h = 5.9 W MacBook average; 100 / (5.9 + 13) = 5.3 h. Video: 100 / (100/24 + 13) = 5.8 h. M5 Max: 100 / (100/16 + 13) = 5.2 h. 13 W is ASUS's stated ceiling ('<13 W'), not a measured typical draw, so real hours should be longer. The sum also assumes the MacBook's own draw does not rise when driving a second display. Battery and hours are Apple's figures.
